                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> At the end of the mobility, your institution has formal procedures for recognising student mobility (good practices linked to recognition at the end of the mobility, e.g. in the use of Transcripts of Records and Grade Distribution Tables)</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Transcripts of Records are issued in a timely manner (normally 5 weeks) to both incoming and outgoing students</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is highly important in the recognition framework to provide Transcripts of Records in a timely manner, immediately following the mobility period. After the mobility, the receiving institution should send a Transcript of Records to the student and to the sending institution within a period stipulated in the Inter-Institutional Agreement (normally within five weeks after publication/proclamation of the student’s results at the receiving institution). It can be provided electronically or through any other means accessible to the student and the sending institution. The Transcript of Records from the receiving institution should refer to the educational components agreed upon in the Learning Agreement. Grade distribution information should be included as well, either as a web link or an annex.</p><p>Following the receipt of the Transcript of Records from the receiving institution, the sending institution should automatically transfer and recognise the student’s academic outcomes successfully completed at the receiving institution, as agreed in the Learning Agreement, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. The Sending Institution will provide a Transcript of Records to the student or record the results in a database or any other means accessible to the student, normally within five weeks after having received the transcript of the receiving institution. The EU official template for the Learning Agreement for studies (including the Transcript of Records) is available online: <a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/opportunities/higher-education/quality-framework_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/opportunities/higher-education/quality-framework_en.htm</a></p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">All credits gained by students during a period of study abroad that were specified in the final version of the Learning Agreement are automatically transferred by your institution and count towards the students' final degree, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The sending institution should ensure that all the credits earned by the mobile student during the mobility period are recognised and counted towards the final degree, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. The period of study abroad must be clear in the student's records and documents issued to the student (Diploma Supplement or equivalent). This is a golden rule of recognition of credit mobility within the framework of inter-institutional agreements. All the credits towards the student's degree that are earned during the mobility period and which were originally agreed on in the Learning Agreement (or a revised version to it) should be recognised by the sending HEI without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. Learning Agreements are binding for all the parties and require that, on successful completion of the mobility period, the sending HEI recognises credits earned by the student and documents these credits in the student records, so they can be identified in a transparent way.</p><p>Upon receipt of the Transcript of Records or Training Certificates, the sending HEI should:<br>a) certify the mobile student has fulfilled all requirements stipulated in the Learning Agreement;<br>b) ensure recognition of the mobility period abroad within the time-scale and according to the conditions stipulated in the institutional recognition framework.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Transcripts of Records of incoming students include a description of or a link to the national grading system</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The Transcript of Records from the receiving institution should include grade distribution information, either as a web link or an annex. The local grading scale should be clearly explained, with a statistical distribution of local grades, to provide transparency and understanding of grading practices at the host institution. Where applicable, use should be made of a Grade Distribution Table for the programme of study, according to the ECTS Users’ Guide (<a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/ects/users-guide/index.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/ects/users-guide/index.htm</a>).</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Grades of outgoing students are converted, if applicable, according to a fair and transparent methodology communicated before the mobility</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Grades of outgoing students are converted, if applicable, according to a fair and transparent methodology communicated before the mobility. There are more details on this in the ECTS Users’ Guide.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">In addition to recognising formal learning, the institution recognises any non-formal or informal learning acquired during the mobility according to the ECTS Users’ Guide, e.g. by awarding ECTS credits for volunteering</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>During a period of mobility, students often take advantage of other opportunities outside of their required courses. These may include specific activities which can be considered non-formal or informal learning where they have acquired new skills. This could include additional language and cultural courses, extra-curricular activities, setting up a business and volunteer work undertaken by the student in that period or upon return at the receiving institution.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/standing-out-from-the-crowd-supporting-students-through-full-recognition-and-documenting-of-mobility-outcomes" target="_blank">"Standing out from the crowd" - supporting students through full recognition and documenting of mobility outcomes</a></div>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/a-common-approach-to-ects-grade-conversion-ensuring-a-fair-assessment-of-student-performance-after-study-abroad" target="_blank">A common approach to ECTS grade conversion, ensuring a fair assessment of student performance after study abroad</a></div>
                                             </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close-text"><i class="fa fa-times fa-2x"></i><span>Close</span></div>
                </div>
            </div>
                         <div class="eche-report-full-question-wrapper">
                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-12.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">12</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q12.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> Your institution issues a Diploma Supplement</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">To all students, automatically, free of charge and in a major European language</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>This Supplement should include a record of the period of mobility under the Erasmus+ Programme. The 48 European countries taking part in the Bologna Process have agreed that each mobile graduate in their respective country should receive the Diploma Supplement (DS) automatically, free of charge and in at least one of the major European languages in addition to the national language. The HEI should issue a Diploma Supplement (or equivalent) to accompany every degree successfully completed by a student, using - where applicable - the template developed by the European Commission, the Council of Europe and UNESCO. The HEI's policy on issuing the Diploma Supplement should be published on its website.</p><p>The template for the Diploma Supplement is available at:<br><a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm&nbsp;</a></p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">That includes a record of the mobility period(s) carried out by the student under the Erasmus+ programme</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The information contained in the Transcript of Records from the Receiving Institution should also be included in the Diploma Supplement produced by the Sending Institution (at least for Sending Institutions located in Programme Countries), with the exact titles of the components that the student has followed abroad. Alongside modules or units taken at the sending HEI, the Diploma Supplement should list recognised modules, units and/or training activities undertaken during the student's mobility period and indicate the location of these mobility activities.<br>In the case of double, multiple or joint degrees, the Diploma Supplement should indicate the name and status of the partner HEIs awarding the degree and explain the respective language(s) of instruction and examination. In addition, an explanation should be provided about the grading and classification scheme agreed by the awarding HEIs. The template for the Diploma Supplement is available at:<br><a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm</a>&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/the-diploma-supplement-a-tool-to-promote-international-recognition-and-transparency-of-academic-achievement" target="_blank">The Diploma Supplement – a tool to promote international recognition and transparency of academic achievement</a></div>
                                             </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close-text"><i class="fa fa-times fa-2x"></i><span>Close</span></div>
                </div>
            </div>
                         <div class="eche-report-full-question-wrapper">
                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-13.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">13</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q13.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> Your institution promotes and recognises staff mobility</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By taking it into account in the assessment of their professional development </span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Participation in international projects should be seen as an important aspect of the professional development of the staff and of the modernisation of the HEI and should, therefore, be considered a key component in staff evaluation practices.</p><p>The HEI should link its HR strategy to the objectives set out the internationalisation strategy for staff. For all staff who undertake a period of mobility, HR should be informed and provide support to ensure the identification of the professional development needs of the individual as well as setting out agreed career objectives for their period of mobility. This can be through prepared addendums to staff contracts or through less formal mechanisms of agreed objectives. The new objectives should become part of the normal system of staff evaluation or appraisal and be used in order to recognise the achievements of the staff during the period of mobility. This means that HR staff should be trained to ensure these additional objectives are formally evidenced and recorded in staff records and lead to other rewards and recognition.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Through, for example the reduction of the teaching load, promotion or pay rises</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is highly important to incentivise staff to participate in mobility activities. In order to support and encourage mobility, HEIs should provide a number of incentives to ensure that when staff return to the sending institution, they have long term career benefits. HEIs should acknowledge periods of mobility as a normal part of a career path. Staff working schedules and agreed objectives (in terms of research outputs and assessments) should be adapted to meet their new requirements. Temporary replacements should be found during the mobility period, where possible, to ensure continuity during the mobility period. Upon returning to the sending institution, incentives to maintain links with other institutions or networks should be put in place through providing the time to nurture new relationships (reduction in teaching or research loads, continued related objectives set in performance appraisals). The new objectives set with HR for the period of mobility should be ones which are explicitly recognised and rewarded through promotion, awards or pay rises. Additional cultural / language skills should be recognised as a component in any evaluation / assessment of the staff. This may be achieved by making it well-known that participation is a formal part of staff evaluation procedures, and may lead to improvements in both working conditions and promotion or broader career prospects.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By encouraging them to propose improvements to the institutional strategy for internationalisation and overarching structure, as well as for structural reform</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>One important form of recognition for staff, which is equally beneficial to the HEI is to encourage their involvement in improving internationalisation and structural reform within the institution. This includes the opportunity for staff to provide feedback into the management structures of departments and the overall institution. There should be a firm commitment - perhaps in writing - from the HEI to recognise and make use of constructive feedback as well as the appropriate forums for staff to engage with senior management to discuss their experiences and propose new ideas for improvement.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By inviting them to share new learning and teaching practices developed abroad with their peers in the institution</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The experience of staff should be valued and shared as an inspiration to others, by, for example, organising meetings and publishing articles where the mobile participants share their experience and the impact of mobility on their personal and professional development. Where staff are involved in teaching at host institutions, new learning and teaching practices can be brought back and shared with other staff members through seminars or presentations. Staff can be supported through the administrative and academic services to understand the skills they have acquired and how best to use them within their own institution.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By encouraging them to propose cooperation projects with their receiving organisation</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Mobile staff bring back new partners, networks and ideas which can be of significant value for the HEI. Staff should be encouraged to propose and develop new or further cooperation projects between their receiving and sending institutions. This requires time and commitment, which need to be given formally by the sending institution, including, for example, additional support to write joint proposals.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/recognition-of-staff-mobility-supporting-individuals-development-and-institutional-aims-and-objectives" target="_blank">Recognition of staff mobility – supporting individuals’ development and institutional aims and objectives</a></div>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/recognition-of-staff-participating-in-erasmus-staff-mobility-actions-and-international-cooperation-projects" target="_blank">Recognition of staff participating in Erasmus staff mobility actions and international cooperation projects</a></div>
                                             </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close-text"><i class="fa fa-times fa-2x"></i><span>Close</span></div>
                </div>
            </div>
                         <div class="eche-report-full-question-wrapper">
                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-14.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">14</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q14.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> With regards to the outcomes and experiences of Erasmus+ activities</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are monitored, evaluated and disseminated as a way to improve international cooperation and mobility activities</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Linked with the overall internationalisation strategy of the institution, monitoring and evaluation of cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility is essential if HEIs are to learn from their experiences. Monitoring and evaluation is more than just measuring the number and types of outputs, it needs to include capturing information on the overall outcomes and experiences of the activities at the institutional and the individual level. Systematic monitoring and evaluation should therefore include more qualitative approaches, which expressly capture the experiences in a way which helps the institution to understand the added value of its involvement in these activities. Documenting and analysing the outcomes and experiences is only the first step. To learn from the approaches taken, and the benefits gained, institutions should take time to disseminate the findings of the cooperation projects and mobility periods through, for example, meetings, workshops and publications, social media, etc. These activities will embed good practice, help the institution to iteratively improve its approach and also feed back into the on-going monitoring and evaluation.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are used systematically for the benefit of your institution, providing internationalisation at home, hence enhancing intercultural competences of non-mobile students and staff</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The outcomes and experiences of cooperation and Erasmus+ mobility have a much wider impact than just improving mobile activities. All institutions have significant numbers of non-mobile staff and students who can benefit from the international experiences of others. As part of the monitoring and evaluation processes, HEIs should consider the impact which can be specifically made on non-mobile staff and students, giving them “internationalisation at home experiences”. This includes building international competences, cultural awareness, virtual mobility opportunities, inviting international lecturers and embedding student projects with an international focus into the curricula, and providing opportunities for local students to work together with incoming mobile participants in e.g. project work, to ensure that local students benefit from the presence of mobile students at their institution. This fits with the activities of disseminating the overall outcomes and experiences of the cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility, though tailored to a different audience. It should take into account the professional development needs of the staff at the HEI and the perspectives of non-mobile students.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are exploited and disseminated, by providing participants with the results of cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility opportunities (e.g. presentations) to share funding possibilities</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The dissemination of outcomes is an integral part of mobility projects. Good practice would be to ensure that the dissemination is built into the support measure and participants in projects and mobility actions are allocated adequate time, resources and space to disseminate their experiences and exploit project results. This includes opportunities to share new knowledge and to highlight new opportunities (including funding) which have arisen from the new relationships formed. In order to do this, HEIs should provide support functions such as web platforms to collect results or opportunities to present results at the institutional or departmental level, as relevant.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">After the mobility Erasmus+ participants have the opportunity to present their newly acquired competences</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The study entitled ‘Effects of mobility on the skills and employability of students and the internationalisation of higher education institutions’ showcases how mobility can contribute to the internationalisation of higher education institutions, including the impacts on teaching methods, cooperation between HEIs and perception of staff more generally. Therefore the dissemination of outcomes is an integral part of mobility projects. Good practice would be to ensure that the dissemination is built into the support measure and participants in projects and mobility actions are allocated adequate time, resources and space to disseminate their experiences and exploit project results. This includes opportunities to share new knowledge and to highlight new opportunities (including funding) which have arisen from the new relationships formed. In order to do this, HEIs should provide support functions such as web platforms to collect results or opportunities to present results at the institutional or departmental level, as relevant.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/capitalising-on-the-outcomes-and-experiences-of-erasmus-activities" target="_blank">Capitalising on the outcomes and experiences of Erasmus+ activities</a></div>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/the-erasmus-impact-study-effects-of-mobility-on-the-skills-and-employability-of-students-and-the-internationalisation-of-higher-education-institutions" target="_blank">The Erasmus Impact Study: Effects of mobility on the skills and employability of students and the internationalisation of higher education institutions</a></div>
                                             </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close-text"><i class="fa fa-times fa-2x"></i><span>Close</span></div>
                </div>
            </div>

About ScholarshipOwl
<\/strong><\/h3>

ScholarshipOwl is the largest scholarship marketplace in the US, using AI to connect 14 million students who are looking for scholarships with companies that are looking for students. Our mission is to make education financing more accessible and engaging, while giving brands a way to connect with the next generation.<\/p>

We\u2019re powered by AI technology that simplifies scholarship discovery, streamlines the application process, and delivers measurable results for both students and partners. Whether it\u2019s helping students secure funding or enabling brands to run impactful campaigns, we\u2019re reshaping how education is funded \u2014 and discovered.<\/p>


<\/span><\/h4>

The Role
<\/strong><\/h3>

We\u2019re looking for a highly skilled and innovative Senior Full-Stack Engineer<\/strong> to architect high-performance web applications and accelerate our development velocity across our B2B platform. You\u2019ll play a pivotal role in bridging modern Nuxt<\/strong> 3\/4 frontend applications\u2014including customer management portals and embeddable widget engines\u2014with a robust Laravel<\/strong> and Doctrine ORM backend API, delivering seamless experiences that connect millions of students to funding opportunities.<\/p>

You will own the technical implementation of core products across our entire stack, working with PHP 8.2+, Laravel, MySQL, and Vue 3 \/ Nuxt 3\/4<\/strong>. Beyond traditional engineering, this role champions efficiency: you will deeply integrate AI-native workflows (using tools like Cursor and Google Gemini) to double shipping velocity, automate test coverage, and build intelligent LLM-driven platform features. If you are passionate about full-stack architecture, widget infrastructure, and leveraging AI to build smarter and faster, this role is for you.<\/p>


<\/span><\/p>

What You\u2019ll Do<\/strong><\/h3>

<\/p>

  • Full Lifecycle Development:<\/strong> Architect, build, and ship end-to-end B2B features across the stack- from Laravel\/Doctrine JSON:API endpoints to reactive Nuxt 3\/4 Vue components and server routes.<\/p><\/li>

  • Embed & Analytics Engine:<\/strong> Develop and optimize high-performance embedded widget systems, Nitro server engine logic, iframe cross-origin messaging, client event-tracking SDKs, and data ingestion pipelines.<\/p><\/li>

  • API & Database Architecture:<\/strong> Design robust relational database schemas (MySQL), Doctrine entity mappings, clean migrations, performant RESTful\/JSON:API contracts, and Redis caching layers.<\/p><\/li>

  • AI-Native Acceleration:<\/strong> Integrate AI coding tools (Cursor, Gemini) into daily development for rapid feature prototyping, code refactoring, test generation, and building LLM-driven product features (e.g., automated applicant evaluation).<\/p><\/li>

  • Third-Party Integrations<\/strong>*:* Integrate and maintain core third-party services and APIs, including CRM platforms, error tracking systems, payment gateways, and cloud data services<\/p><\/li>

  • Automated Testing & Quality:<\/strong> Establish comprehensive automated test coverage (PHPUnit for backend, Playwright and Vitest for E2E\/components) integrated into CI\/CD pipelines to guarantee zero regressions.<\/p><\/li>

  • Mentorship & Code Reviews:<\/strong> Conduct thorough, constructive code reviews and collaborate closely with product managers, QA engineers, and leadership to elevate team standards.<\/p><\/li><\/ul>

    <\/h4>

    Required Qualifications (Must Haves)<\/h3>

    <\/p>

    • Experience:<\/strong> 4+ years of professional full-stack web development experience, with at least 1+ year actively incorporating AI coding assistants into daily engineering workflows.<\/p><\/li>

    • Backend Expertise (PHP & Laravel):<\/strong> Strong commercial experience with PHP 8+ and Laravel (clean service architecture, queues\/jobs, middleware, and OAuth2\/Passport authentication).<\/p><\/li>

    • Frontend Mastery (Vue 3 & Nuxt 3\/4):<\/strong> Deep proficiency in modern Vue 3 (Composition API), Nuxt 3 or Nuxt 4, TypeScript, Pinia state management, and Tailwind CSS.<\/p><\/li>

    • Database & ORM Skills:<\/strong> Strong relational database modeling and query optimization in MySQL, along with solid experience using ORMs (Doctrine ORM \/ DBAL or deep Eloquent experience with the ability to adapt to Doctrine quickly).<\/p><\/li>

    • API Design & Caching:<\/strong> Deep understanding of RESTful \/ JSON:API standards, server-side validation error mapping, request formatting, and Redis performance caching.<\/p><\/li>

    • AI-Native Workflow:<\/strong> Active daily use of AI coding tools (Cursor, Gemini) as a force multiplier for coding, debugging, and test creation.<\/p><\/li>

    • Automated Testing:<\/strong> Hands-on experience writing backend test suites (PHPUnit) and frontend\/E2E tests (Playwright, Vitest, or Cypress).<\/p><\/li>

    • DevOps & Tooling:<\/strong> Solid working knowledge of Git, CI\/CD release pipelines, Docker containerization, and Linux\/container environments.<\/p><\/li>

    • Async Communication & Autonomy:<\/strong> Exceptional written technical communication skills for authoring PRs, architectural design docs, and issue tracking; high autonomy to navigate multi-service codebases, solve complex blockers independently, and drive initiatives.<\/p><\/li><\/ul>

      <\/p>

      Good to Have<\/h3>

      <\/p>

      • Education & Background:<\/strong> Bachelor\u2019s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or equivalent practical software engineering experience.<\/p><\/li>

      • Certifications<\/strong>*:* Advanced degree or formal certifications in Cloud Architecture, Modern Software Engineering, or AI Engineering.<\/p><\/li>

      • Doctrine ORM:<\/strong> Direct production experience with Doctrine ORM \/ DBAL in Laravel environments.<\/p><\/li>

      • Widget & SDK Systems:<\/strong> Experience developing embeddable web widgets, lightweight JavaScript tracking SDKs, iframe cross-origin communication, or browser fingerprinting.<\/p><\/li>

      • Modern Tooling:<\/strong> Experience with Nitro server engines, Bun runtime, PrimeVue components, or streaming data into data warehouses (e.g., BigQuery).<\/p><\/li>

      • Payment Gateways:<\/strong> Integration experience with payment processors (Stripe\/Braintree) and B2B subscription billing lifecycles.<\/p><\/li>

      • Gemini LLM Integration:<\/strong> Practical experience integrating Google Gemini models (prompt engineering, structured JSON outputs, Gemini API \/ SDKs).<\/p><\/li>

      • Cloud Infrastructure (GCP):<\/strong> Hands-on experience with Google Cloud Platform (Cloud Run, Kubernetes, Cloud Build).<\/p>

        <\/p>

        Bonus Skills (The \"X-Factor\")<\/h3>

        <\/p>

        • Technical Leadership:<\/strong> Prior experience in a Tech Lead or Team Lead capacity\u2014driving architectural decisions, coordinating delivery, and unblocking team members.<\/p><\/li>

        • Domain Knowledge:<\/strong> Background in high-growth B2B SaaS platforms, grant\/applicant management systems, EdTech, recruitment\/ATS tools, or conversion tracking ecosystems.<\/p><\/li>

        • Product-Minded Execution:<\/strong> Strong product ownership mindset\u2014evaluating engineering trade-offs through the lens of user experience, conversion funnel impact, and tangible business value.<\/p><\/li><\/ul>


          <\/span><\/p><\/li><\/ul>

          Why Join ScholarshipOwl?
          <\/span><\/h3>

          • Mission-Driven Work:<\/strong> Build technology that helps students unlock education opportunities and reduce financial barriers.<\/p><\/li>

          • Fully Remote:<\/strong> Work from anywhere in the world while collaborating with a global team.<\/p><\/li>

          • High Impact & Ownership:<\/strong> You aren't just a cog in a machine; you own your domain and directly drive results.<\/p><\/li>

          • Unlimited PTO:<\/strong> We value outcomes over hours worked and trust you to manage your time.<\/p><\/li>

          • Computer Upgrade Budget:<\/strong> Up to $1,600 to invest in your ideal primary work computer.<\/p><\/li>

Senior Project Manager, Marketing PMO

As a Senior Project Manager on Intapp’s Marketing PMO team, you will lead complex, high-priority, cross-functional marketing initiatives from planning through completion while helping mature how the Marketing organization plans and delivers work. You will bring structure to ambiguity, facilitate collaboration across teams, drive accountability, and ensure projects deliver against their intended outcomes. This role is ideal for an experienced project leader who combines strong PM fundamentals with the judgment, initiative, and communication skills to independently drive complex work and know when to escalate.

What you will do

  • Lead complex projects end-to-end: Own high-visibility, cross-functional marketing initiatives, translating business objectives into clear scope, plans, milestones, deliverables, owners, dependencies, and timelines. Manage scope and changes throughout the project lifecycle and apply the appropriate level of project management rigor based on the complexity and needs of the initiative.
  • Drive execution, governance, and accountability: Establish and maintain appropriate project governance, facilitate working sessions and project meetings, identify next steps, manage risks and issues, resolve blockers, and keep teams moving toward outcomes. Independently address issues where appropriate and escalate material risks or decisions to the Director, Marketing PMO with clear context, options, and recommendations.
  • Partner across the organization: Collaborate with Marketing, Creative, Product Marketing, Demand Generation, Events, Communications, Operations, and other stakeholders to align priorities and drive accountability without direct authority. Work closely with other PMs to create consistency and share effective practices across the team.
  • Strengthen PMO processes and methodology: Help develop and mature project management methodology, governance, templates, documentation, and standards. Identify gaps and inefficiencies, implement practical improvements, and use lessons learned to continuously improve how projects are planned and delivered.
  • Create visibility and institutional knowledge: Manage projects in Asana and other PM tools, maintain accurate project plans, risks, issues, decisions, actions, and status, and provide clear, actionable reporting. Ensure project outcomes, decisions, and lessons learned are captured to build institutional knowledge and support a consistent, scalable PMO.

What you will need

Intapp is looking for intellectually curious, self-motivated professionals who like to get hands-on to contribute to the overall success of the business and their team. To apply for this Senior Project Manager role, you will ideally have:

  • Strong project management fundamentals and demonstrated experience independently leading complex, cross-functional projects from initiation through completion.
  • A track record of taking ownership, anticipating next steps, solving problems, managing scope and change, and driving projects forward rather than simply tracking activity.
  • Strong facilitation, communication, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence and create accountability across teams and work effectively with senior stakeholders.
  • Experience creating structure in ambiguous or evolving environments and improving project management processes, methodologies, governance, and ways of working.
  • Experience in a marketing, creative, agency, technology, professional services, SaaS, or similarly complex environment, along with familiarity with Asana or comparable project management tools.

Ready for a challenge?

Then Just Eat Takeaway.com might be the place for you. We’re a leading global online delivery platform, and our vision is to empower everyday convenience.

Whether it’s a Friday-night feast, a post-gym poke bowl, or grabbing some groceries, our tech platform connects tens of millions of customers with hundreds of thousands of restaurant, grocery and convenience partners across the globe.


About this role


We are looking for a Senior Java Developer to join our Logistics Areas and Fees team. If you are passionate about building scalable, high-throughput backend services and thrive in a fast-paced, high-scale environment, this role is for you. This role is open to candidates based in Toronto, Montreal, Ottawa or Winnipeg.


As a Senior Java Developer within our Logistics domain, you will play a key role in architecting, developing, and operating the core services and distributed systems that power delivery areas & fees related calculations. You will own backend systems end-to-end, from system architecture and API design to deployment, observability, and performance optimization, ensuring high availability and low-latency execution across our platform.


Your mission is to deliver robust, performant, and resilient Java-based services, working closely with cross-functional teams of engineers, product managers, and data analysts to ship critical backend infrastructure that our internal operators and the wider logistics platform rely on every day. You will champion modern Java standards, system reliability, and software engineering best practices, while mentoring team members and helping shape the technical direction of backend engineering within the organization.


In short, you’ll combine deep Java and backend expertise with a strong system design mindset to power mission-critical logistics operations at scale.


Location: Remote - Alberta, Manitoba, Ontario

Reporting to: Technology Manager

These are some of the key components of the position:

  • Maintain existing and develop new microservices using Java 21. Extend the functionality of existing applications per Business requests.
  • Maintain existing and develop new infrastructure resources on the AWS platform using Terraform.
  • Work with a microservices architecture using REST API and Message Brokers.
  • Design, build, and maintain high-performance, scalable backend services and APIs using Java.
  • Participate in architectural decisions, RFCs, and technical design reviews across the Logistics domain
  • Collaborate with Product, QE, and Data colleagues to ship high-quality releases on a continuous delivery cadence
  • Own your work throughout the entire product development lifecycle, from technical design and planning to market release.
  • Review the code of peers in a team.
  • Support and mentor team members, helping grow backend engineering as a discipline
  • Identify improvements, highlight risks vs benefits, and translate them into technical requirements.
  • Work with the product team, providing technical knowledge and expertise, helping to design the future of our products.
  • Participate in paid on-call rotation.

What will you bring to the team?

  • 7+ years of hands-on experience architecting and building scalable, high-performance enterprise applications and leading complex software development projects.
  • Be curious, with a strong appetite for new knowledge.
  • Strong software engineering fundamentals, including data structures, design patterns, testing, and debugging.
  • Solid understanding of consuming, producing, and designing RESTful web services.
  • Experience with Java (Spark or Quarkus framework).
  • Experience with streams and list operations is a nice-to-have.
  • Solid grounding in design patterns for designing distributed systems (bounded contexts, sagas, eventual consistency, and the outbox pattern) (must have).
  • Experience in Domain-Driven Design (DDD) is a strong nice-to-have.
  • Experience with message brokers (Kafka, Amazon SQS, RabbitMQ).
  • Production experience deploying to AWS and running services on Kubernetes (EKS).Experience with System logging and monitoring using tools such as Grafana, AWS CloudWatch and DataDog.
  • Experience with data persistence in relational, MySQL, unstructured and/or cached forms.
  • Strong experience with Redis for caching, rate limiting and distributed locks is a plus.
  • Knowledge of Infrastructure-as-a-Code (Terraform) is nice-to-have.
  • Understanding of continuous delivery, deployment, and integration.
  • Familiarity with Version Control (Git) and related tools.

AI & Modern Engineering Capabilities

  • Hands-on experience with AI-assisted development tools such as Cursor, Claude Code, Codex or similar is required
  • Experience making repositories agent-ready, maintaining clear in-repo documentation, AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md files, structured code conventions, and reproducible local setups so AI coding agents can contribute effectively
  • Experience using AI agents to drive end-to-end engineering tasks (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor agents, or similar) for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and automated PR workflows
  • Experience integrating AI into backend engineering workflows (e.g., AI-assisted code review, test generation, log/incident analysis, intelligent on-call triage)
  • Understanding of prompt engineering and evaluation of AI-generated outputs in a software engineering context
  • Awareness of best practices for AI-driven development, including reliability, reproducibility, security, and governance, particularly as they apply to production backend systems

At JET, this is on the menu:

Our teams forge connections internally and work with some of the best-known brands on the planet, giving us truly international impact in a dynamic environment.

Fun, fast-paced and supportive, the JET culture is about movement, growth and about celebrating every aspect of our JETers. Thanks to them we stay one step ahead of the competition.

No matter who you are, what you look like, who you love, or where you are from, you can find your place at Just Eat Takeaway.com. Digital Nomads: Family abroad or just want a change of scenery? Enjoy the freedom to work from almost anywhere in the world for 4 weeks a year.

Career Growth: Fuel your personal and professional evolution through our dedicated mentorship, global mobility pathways, and a wellness-first culture rooted in true diversity and inclusion.

Corporate Travel Consultant (AMDOC Team)

FCM takes a holistic approach to corporate travel, specializing in managing national and global travel programs for medium and large businesses.

Ranked as one of the world’s top five travel management companies, it has a business network in over 97 countries and global headquarters in London, Brisbane, Singapore and New York. Backed by the global strength of Flight Centre Travel Group (FCTG), FCM combines local expertise and global experience to provide clients with a truly bespoke experience.

To learn more about FCM please click HERE

About the Opportunity

This role will have you arranging domestic and complex international travel for busy executives including air, car hotel and ground transportation. Before you begin your role, you will spend four weeks (paid). This program will boost your knowledge, train you on contract airfares and sharpen your Sabre skills. Our corporate travel agents handle the air, car, rail and ground transportation bookings as well as the ticketing, changes and the exchange and queue management.  You will also need to offer exceptional customer service to satisfy our business traveler’s needs. We encourage our Corporate Travel Agents to study the travel polices of our corporate accounts and develop a relationship with them so when our valued business travelers have the need for business travel arrangements, they rest assured that their business travel needs are in the hands of a dedicated team of Corporate Travel professionals they trust and are on a first name basis with.

Our business hours are 8:00 AM to 8:00 PM EST Monday – Friday

A typical schedule will include a 40-hour work week with five 8-hour shifts. Be prepared to work an evening shift until 8:00 PM once or twice a week.

Key Responsibilities

  • Coordinate air, hotel, car, and ground transportation bookings for domestic and international travel
  • Build rapport and develop a relationship with business travelers to ensure their business travel needs are in the hands of a trusted team of Corporate Travel professionals
  • Ensure accurate and timely completion of reservations while meeting travelers' needs
  • Executing all responsibilities within company guidelines for customer service, documentation of PNRS (Passenger Name Records) and profiles, ticketing, invoicing, and maintaining accuracy throughout
  • Staying fully informed about airline rules, regulations, tariffs, and fare requirements and applying this knowledge accurately to all travel arrangements
  • Deliver consultative support and exceptional customer service throughout the booking process
  • Keeping clients informed about all necessary travel documents and health requirements for their destinations
  • Proficiently handling ticketing, Phase IVs, and exchanges/changes involving complex international fares
  • Expertly managing rerouting and exchange processes, ensuring minimal disruption to travel plans
  • Other duties and tasks as assigned
  • Contribute to a safe, inclusive, and accessible work environment where all Flighties feel welcomed, respected, and supported to thrive

Experience & Qualifications

  • 2+ years of recent, prior experience in corporate travel management, understanding the unique needs and challenges of business travelers.
  • In-depth familiarity with current Sabre GDS (Global Distribution System) for fare calculations, itinerary management, and ticket issuance.
  • Previous exposure to quality control processes to ensure the accuracy and compliance of travel bookings.
  • Proficiency in ticketing procedures and scripting, along with the ability to handle complex itinerary changes and exchanges for both international and domestic travel.
  • Proven ability to navigate and manipulate complex itineraries, international fares, and Passenger Name Records (PNRs) to meet client requirements.
  • A polished and professional demeanor when interacting with clients and colleagues.
  • Proficiency in handling multiple urgent tasks simultaneously while maintaining efficiency and quality in each interaction.
  • The capacity to make quick and effective decisions to resolve travel-related issues promptly.
  • Excellent communication skills to keep clients informed and reassured throughout the travel process.
  • A deep commitment to delivering exceptional customer service with a focus on client satisfaction.
  • Comfortable and proficient in using travel booking systems and various communication tools.
  • Strong technical aptitude with the ability to troubleshoot and adapt to new technologies
  • Self-motivated with the ability to work independently and manage tasks successfully
  • Reliable, high-speed internet connectivity required to support core job responsibilities, including but not limited to video conferencing, access to company systems, and secure handling of company data.

Work Perks! - What’s in it for you:

FCTG is renowned internationally for having amazing perks and an even better culture. We understand that our people are our most valuable asset. It is the passion and dedication of our teams that keep the company on top of the industry ladder. It’s also why we offer some great employee benefits and perks outside of the norm.

  • Have fun:At the heart of everything we do at Flight Centre is a desire to have fun.

  • We back our people all the way: We are strongly committed to supporting every single employee in their professional and personal development.
  • Giving Back:Our Corporate Social Responsibility program supports nominated charities through volunteering and fundraising, complemented by our Office Environmental Program, LEED® Gold-certified office spaces, and 1 paid Volunteer Day per calendar year.

NeoWork is hiring a Restaurant Catering Account Manager for a fully remote contractor engagement with a bilingual restaurant consulting firm in the United States. The firm helps independent restaurants add corporate catering as a second line of business, supported by digital marketing, training and operations manuals, and guidance through zoning and liquor permit processes. The contractor manages a book of up to 18 restaurant clients and reports directly to the firm’s owner.

Role overview

You will meet with each client for a 60-minute working session every week by video and screen share. Between sessions, you will do the work that keeps each client’s catering program growing, including building and maintaining catering assets, tracking performance against each client’s targets, and bringing issues or opportunities to the owner as they arise. This is a self-directed role that requires strong organization across many clients at once.

Responsibilities

  • Lead weekly 60-minute sessions with each client in English or Spanish.
  • Build and update catering menus, per-person pricing, and catering listings.
  • Keep each client’s Google Business Profile and website current.
  • Write catering procedures, packing guides, and staff training materials.
  • Prepare forms and applications for clients to review, sign, and submit themselves. The contractor never signs documents on a client’s behalf.
  • Guide clients through local zoning and state liquor permit processes, with the client completing and submitting each application. The contractor provides procedural support only and does not provide legal, financial, or tax advice. Those questions are referred to the client’s own professionals.
  • Track orders and weekly meal volume, and help each client reach their catering targets.
  • Keep a session log after every meeting recording the actions taken by the contractor, the actions taken by the client, and any documents the client signed.
  • Escalate problems, opportunities, and SEO or social media requests to the owner promptly. SEO and social media work is handled by a separate team member, so these requests route through the owner.
  • Work through delegated user access to client accounts. The contractor does not handle client passwords, Social Security numbers, or bank details, and treats all client information and methods as confidential.

Requirements

  • Fluent written and spoken English.
  • Professional Spanish, strongly preferred.
  • At least two years of experience in account management, client success, or marketing, ideally with restaurants, hospitality, or small businesses.
  • An MBA or equivalent business experience at that level.
  • Comfort with Google Workspace, video meetings, CRM tools, and website editors.
  • Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage many clients without close supervision.
  • Full-time availability during U.S. Eastern business hours, with client sessions mainly scheduled between 9:30 and 11:00 a.m. and 2:00 and 4:30 p.m. ET. Candidates in other time zones must confirm they can cover these windows.

Nice to have

  • Restaurant or food service experience.
  • Experience with online ordering or catering platforms.
  • Graphic design or menu design skills.

Benefits

  • We offer health insurance for contractors
  • Holiday Extra Pay
  • The work hours generally align with standard business hours in the US, with some potential flexibility depending on the client's needs.
  • This is a 100% home-based position
  • We prioritize the mental health of our team members and offer mental health days to support their well-being.
  • In addition to the base salary, performance-based incentives are provided.
  • There is an annual review and appraisal process in place.
  • There are ample opportunities for professional growth and advancement within the company.

Overview

Are you ready to make a difference in the world of consumer finance? At Attain Finance, we bring over 50 years of expertise in providing credit solutions across the U.S. and Canada. Our deep roots in the financial industry have empowered us to develop convenient, easily accessible financial services that meet our customers' growing needs.

Join a leading consumer credit lender that thrives on innovation and collaboration, where your contributions are truly valued. Our portfolio includes distinguished brands like Cash Money®, LendDirect® and Heights Finance. Each brand is constantly evolving to better serve our customers.

Be part of a dynamic team that is shaping the future of consumer finance. Apply today and take the next step in your career with Attain Finance!

Responsibilities

The Dialer Administrator is responsible for the day-to-day administration, configuration, and operational support of the organization’s enterprise outbound dialer platform. This role ensures dialing strategies and customer contact activities are reliable, secure, and compliant, and effectively support Collections, Customer Service, Sales, and other business functions. The position serves as the primary subject-matter expert for campaign configuration, dialing strategies, routing logic, data integration, reporting, and production support, working closely with business stakeholders, Technology, Compliance, Legal, Workforce Management, Contact Center Operations, and external vendors to ensure outbound communications are executed accurately and in accordance with regulatory and internal requirements.

  • Administer and maintain the enterprise outbound dialer platform, including users, security roles, permissions, access controls, and platform settings.
  • Build, configure, test, and deploy outbound campaigns, dialing strategies, routing rules, and queues using predictive, progressive, preview, and manual dialing methodologies based on business requirements.
  • Maintain calling windows, time-zone controls, campaign priorities, pacing, retry logic, and contact rules.
  • Manage campaign lists and validate data, segmentation, suppression criteria, and file accuracy prior to deployment; ensure required approvals are obtained through established change management processes.
  • Ensure dialing campaigns are configured and executed in accordance with TCPA, FDCPA, and other applicable requirements, including controls for consent, contact frequency, Do Not Call requests, and suppression rules.
  • Maintain accurate records of campaign configurations, approvals, controls, and system changes; support internal and external compliance audits and partner with Compliance and Legal to implement required changes.
  • Monitor platform performance, campaign execution, system capacity, and data processing; investigate and resolve failed loads, dialing errors, routing issues, and integration failures.
  • Work with platform providers and vendors to resolve technical issues; support incident management and root-cause analysis, and escalate significant issues to the appropriate Technology or business teams.
  • Produce recurring operational and campaign performance reports and dashboards, monitoring key metrics such as contact rate, right-party contact rate, abandonment rate, agent occupancy, penetration rate, and conversion or resolution rate.
  • Analyze campaign performance and operational trends to recommend improvements to dialing strategies, pacing, routing, contact strategies, and automation.
  • Support platform upgrades, releases, new functionality, integrations, and user acceptance testing; maintain accurate platform configuration and operating documentation.
  • Participate in production support and after-hours escalation processes as required.
  • Complete additional duties and projects assigned by leadership.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Marketing, Communications, Information Systems, or a related discipline preferred.
  • Minimum of 5 years of experience in customer communications, digital engagement, contact center strategy, operations, or process optimization.
  • Experience managing SMS communication programs or digital customer engagement strategies preferred.
  • Experience with Five9 or comparable contact center platforms is considered an asset.
  • Experience in financial services, consumer finance, or regulated industries preferred.
  • Demonstrated experience leading cross-functional initiatives and process improvement projects.

Core Competencies

  • Platform administration and campaign configuration expertise
  • Knowledge of predictive, progressive, preview, and manual dialing strategies
  • Technical troubleshooting, root-cause analysis, system testing, and validation skills
  • Understanding of APIs, system integrations, data interfaces, and workflow concepts
  • Data analysis, reporting, and performance-monitoring capabilities
  • Attention to regulatory and compliance requirements, including consent, calling windows, contact preferences, and Do Not Call controls
  • Awareness of data privacy, information security, documentation, and governance requirements
  • Attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple campaigns and competing priorities
  • Organizational and time management skills under time-sensitive deadlines
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical issues in clear business language
  • Stakeholder management and collaboration with technical and non-technical teams
  • Process and continuous improvement mindset

Working Conditions

  • Schedule: Monday-Friday, 7:00 AM-4:00 PM EST, additional evening and weekend hours may be required based on business needs

    On-Call: Rotating schedule of one week on, one week off. Availability for after-hours support is required

  • Hybrid or remote work arrangement based on business needs
  • Occasional travel may be required for project meetings, vendor engagements, or company events

Base Salary: $55,000 - $70,000 USD

The actual base salary offered for this full-time position will be determined by various factors, including but not limited to, location, skills, knowledge, competencies, and experience.

Overview

In response to the recently passed Workplace Gender Equality Amendment (Closing the Gender Pay Gap) Bill 2023 in March, a Reform Delivery Project (RDP) is formed to deliver the required changes. The identified requirement under REC2: Publishing GPG > Platform to Publish GPGs, will require the changes in our data explorer that we generally share our insights with the general public.

The data explorer which is built in Tableau, accessible at our WGEA website will provide the following

  • The insights published will be grouped into 6 Gender Equality Indicators at National, Industry, and Employer level with filters in sub-division (ANZSIC), group (ANZSIC), class (ANZSIC), or business size.
    • Gender Pay Gap (GPG)
    • Workforce Composition
    • Boards and Governing Bodies
    • Employer action to improve: Policies and strategies, flexible work, domestic violence support, parental leave & support for carers.
    • Sexual harassment and discrimination
    • Employee consultation
  • The data explorer should provide a page where it allows the user to compare the data between industry, and employers.
  • The data explorer will also provide secondary page to preselect data points for data extractions for their own analysis.
  • Each employer GPG commentary, website link.
  • The public report will remain unchanged.

The procurement service is required to engage tableau and insight developer to deliver the above requirements by two phases Nov 2023 (regular annual release) and early 2024 (new GPG release). 3. Can do attitude in exploring and stretching limitations to fulfil most of our reporting needs in a non-negotiable delivery timeline. 20 %

Overview

Ferrellgas is looking for a Reconciliation Support Specialist to join the team! This role is responsible for supporting daily cash application activities, researching unapplied funds, and assisting with the resolution of payment discrepancies, including overpayments and misapplied payments. This position works collaboratively with internal teams and customers to ensure accurate and timely payment processing, maintain appropriate documentation, and support account reconciliation activities.

Why You’ll Love Working Here

At Ferrellgas, we’re committed to supporting our team with benefits that promote health, financial security, and personal growth:

  • Comprehensive Health Coverage: Medical, dental, vision, accident, and critical illness insurance
  • Income Protection: Company-provided short-term and long-term disability, life insurance, and AD&D
  • Financial Wellness: 401(k) with company match, Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP), Flexible Spending Account (FSA), and Health Savings Account (HSA)
  • Time Off & Family Support: Paid Time Off (PTO), parental leave, and tuition reimbursement
  • Wellness & Assistance Programs: Wellness program, Employee Assistance Program (EAP), and Medicare support
  • Employee Perks: Referral program, employee discount programs, and propane savings

Responsibilities

  • Posts daily incoming cash.
  • Creates payment loaders for larger customers.
  • Researches unapplied payments and assists with resolving discrepancies in collaboration with team members.
  • Researches and resolves cash application issues.
  • Communicates with customers regarding unapplied payments and related inquiries.
  • Researches overpayments.
  • Responds to customer inquiries regarding any payment application issue.
  • Investigates routine payment discrepancies and works toward timely resolution.
  • Assists with audit requests by gathering payment records and reconciliation documentation.

Qualifications

  • Associate degree in accounting or related field preferred.
  • 1+ years of related work experience.
  • Able to interact professionally with internal and external Ferrellgas customers.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel).
  • Excellent communication (written and verbal) and interpretation skills.
  • Detail oriented and highly organized.
  • Salesforce/PeopleSoft/Navision Great plains experience preferred.
  • Must be a Citizen or National of the United States, a lawful, permanent resident, or have authorization to work in the United States.
  • Applicants must not now, or any time in the future, require sponsorship for an employment visa.

Why work for Ferrellgas?

We pride ourselves in providing the best customer service in the propane industry. Ranked consistently as one of the top propane suppliers in the country, Ferrellgas is in the business of providing meaningful moments. Memories full of warmth, dependability you can trust, and outcomes you had only dreamed possible.

Ferrellgas has been recognized by Forbes as one of the Best Employers in America. Please visit our Life at Ferrellgas page for more information.
